title: Declarative partitioning: by range, by list and by hash

videos.script: Every night a job deletes the oldest month of events. It used to take a minute. Now it takes an hour, and the site is slow while it runs. {{nightly}} A delete is the expensive way to remove a month. Every row is marked dead, every change is written to the log, and the cleaner has to come back for all of it. {{delete}} Partitioning is the other way. One table name, and behind it one real table per month. {{partitions}} Removing a month becomes dropping a table. In this lesson that is fifty-five kilobytes of log instead of two hundred and fifty megabytes. {{drop}} You build the events table again, cut by month, and route five million rows into it. Then two other cuts, by list and by hash, and the trap each one hides. {{kinds}} You attach a month prepared in advance, detach one without blocking, and meet the default partition and its price. {{attach}} And you meet the rules a partitioned table imposes, on primary keys and on indexes. {{keys}} One warning runs through all of it. Partitioning is for maintenance. A query that does not name the partition key gets slower, not faster. {{warning}}
